# Host tools — the in-app browser

- `browser_*` (the in-app browser, root `AGENTS.md` → *Constraints*, item 8; `BrowserBroker` over `v1/browser`): seventeen tools that drive the chat's tabs in Electron main; an agent names and colours each tab it opens (`browser_open` `name` / `color`, `browser_label_tab`), and a name or colour the user set on a tab is never overwritten by an agent (main's `BrowserService.labelTab`). `v1/browser` is a leaf module — `BrowserBridgeService` (every desktop socket that sent the gateway's `browser_host` is remembered, most recent first, and forgotten on its disconnect; a paired device's is refused; `browser_request` goes to the most recent one still connected, by socket id only, never a room, so a second desktop client leaving hands the browser back to the window; a request fails at once when no desktop socket is connected (`BROWSER_NO_WINDOW_REASON`, which never claims the window is closed), after `BROWSER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (20 s, well inside cursor's fixed 60 s tool deadline), on abort, on the disconnect of the socket it went to and on the run's teardown) and `BrowserHostApprovals` (in memory per run). The CLI permission for every `browser_*` call is auto-approved in every mode (`isHostBrowserCall`, the chat's `autoApproves` and the team executor's in-turn arm): the question is the tool's own new-host card. Outside `auto`, `browser_open` / `browser_navigate` to a host the chat has not approved raise a DEFERRED `approval_request` (`toolName: 'browser_host'`, input `{host, url, memberName}`) and answer at once; the verdict (Approve, Allow for this session as `optionId: 'session'`, Deny) records the host, runs the operation and wakes the agent through `HostWakeBus`. A navigation an operation causes may only reach the hosts the request carries (`allowedHosts`, null in `auto` or after Allow for this session). The sink stays registered past the turn (`keepHostTools`). Team members get the same sink and share their run's tabs and jar. Cookie values an agent sets are masked in the persisted `tool_call` row by `event-to-item` and registered with the redactor first — whatever sits under a `cookies` key, in any shape, so a call the tool refuses is masked too — and a value of 8 characters or more is masked again where a page prints it back into a browser tool's result (or a result whose CLI names no tool, claude); `browser_get_cookies` never returns a value. `browser_screenshot` saves the png at full resolution as a run attachment and names its path in the text (the transcript's card draws it from that path); it adds an MCP image part (`McpToolResult.images`) only on `view: true`, and that copy is main's second capture at CSS-pixel scale (`clip.scale = 1/devicePixelRatio`, `viewPng`), since a picture in the result is what costs the agent's context. `width` / `height` take the shot under `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` and clear it after, the capture failing or not. `browser_snapshot` answers the element tree alone by default; `interactive: true` keeps only the actionable roles, `text: true` adds the page's visible text in its untrusted fence, and the tool's `PAGE_CONTENT_PREFACE` is the one warning. The gateway takes socket messages up to `BROWSER_REPLY_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB) for a screenshot reply, and main refuses one whose pictures together pass `BROWSER_SCREENSHOT_MAX_BASE64`.
